hypotheses.statement: In adults spanning the full range of skin pigmentation, calibrated 350–650 nm UPE emitted 1–3 minutes after a standardized suberythemal UVA exposure will add at least 0.10 to out-of-sample R² for predicting 24-hour erythema beyond UVA dose, baseline erythema, skin lightness, skin temperature and perfusion.

scope.population: Adults with prospectively balanced skin-lightness strata
scope.condition: Standardized suberythemal solar-simulated UVA exposure after controlled acclimation and dark adaptation
scope.comparator: Prediction model containing UVA dose, baseline colorimetry, skin lightness L*, temperature and perfusion but no UPE
scope.outcome: Change in colorimeter-measured erythema a* at 24 hours

hypotheses.null_hypothesis: The cross-validated incremental R² from adding 1–3-minute UPE is less than 0.10, or its bootstrap 95% confidence interval includes zero.
hypotheses.estimand: ΔR² = R²clinical+UPE − R²clinical in a locked external-validation cohort.

rationale.step: UV-induced UPE averaged over 1–3 minutes increased with dose and was highly correlated with cutaneous redness 24 hours later; accompanying cell experiments linked the signal to lipid peroxidation.
UVA-induced UPE depends on skin lightness and persists for up to two hours, making pigmentation a load-bearing covariate rather than a demographic nuisance variable.
Clinical UPE measurement is vulnerable to thermal and optical confounds and lacks standardized protocols.
For each held-out participant, compute predictions from nested models and calculate ΔR²; the hypothesis survives only if ΔR²≥0.10 and the participant-bootstrap 95% confidence interval excludes zero.

hypotheses.proposed_experiment: Pre-register a multicentre dose-response study with a locked acquisition window, sham-exposed neighboring skin, photon-reference calibration, blinded 24-hour colorimetry and a completely held-out validation centre; fit the clinical model first and add only the pre-specified background-subtracted 1–3-minute photon radiance.
hypotheses.required_instrument: Calibrated photon-counting photomultiplier or cooled EMCCD covering 350–650 nm in a light-tight chamber, plus a skin colorimeter, thermometer and perfusion monitor.
hypotheses.novelty_self_claim: This advances beyond H8 by testing a provoked, temporally fixed UPE measurement against a future clinical photodamage endpoint across pigmentation strata rather than associating baseline surface UPE with generic systemic oxidative status.

hypotheses.statement: In adults with type 2 diabetes starting a glucose-lowering regimen, the week-2 change in the hand-UPE photon-count ratio 495–550 nm/550–610 nm will add at least 0.10 to out-of-sample R² for predicting 12-week HbA1c reduction beyond baseline HbA1c, medication class, BMI and total UPE intensity.

scope.population: Adults with type 2 diabetes initiating or intensifying a stable glucose-lowering regimen
scope.condition: Bilateral hand UPE measured before treatment and at week 2 under identical circadian, dark-adaptation and environmental conditions
scope.comparator: Clinical prediction model using baseline HbA1c, medication class, BMI and broadband UPE intensity without the spectral ratio
scope.outcome: Laboratory-measured change in HbA1c from baseline to week 12

hypotheses.null_hypothesis: Adding the week-2 spectral-ratio change produces incremental cross-validated R² below 0.10 or a 95% confidence interval including zero.
hypotheses.estimand: Incremental external-validation R² attributable to Δlog[(495–550 nm counts)/(550–610 nm counts)].

rationale.step: In treated type 2 diabetes patients, UPE intensity changed over two weeks and the 495–550 nm/550–610 nm ratio was negatively correlated with contemporaneous syndrome scores.
Separate human studies report UPE differences between people with type 2 diabetes and healthy controls and propose UPE for early-stage diabetes detection.
Plasma metabolomics work in pre-diabetes linked UPE-based subtyping to lipid-profile differences, providing a biochemical candidate source of diabetes-related optical variation.
An analytical review specifically recommends combining spectral information with intensity, using larger populations and applying statistical validation.

Calculate the log spectral ratio at both visits, subtract baseline from week 2, and compare locked nested models in held-out patients; ΔR²≥0.10 with a positive lower confidence bound is the decision rule.

hypotheses.proposed_experiment: Run a pre-registered prospective cohort alongside routine diabetes treatment, with fixed hand sites and blinded HbA1c assays; train the model in two clinics and test it without refitting in a third clinic.
hypotheses.required_instrument: Calibrated cooled photon-counting PMT with 495–550 nm and 550–610 nm bandpass channels plus a 400–650 nm broadband channel.
hypotheses.novelty_self_claim: The registered claims do not test whether an early UPE spectral change forecasts a later objective biochemical treatment response; this replaces contemporaneous subjective syndrome correlation with prospective HbA1c prediction.

hypotheses.statement: In patients with erythropoietic protoporphyria, the calibrated initial 350–650 nm UPE burst following a standardized low-dose solar-simulated exposure will improve prediction of the 24-hour phototoxic skin reaction by at least 0.10 AUC beyond erythrocyte protoporphyrin IX, plasma iron, exposure dose and skin lightness.

scope.population: Adolescents and adults with biochemically or genetically confirmed erythropoietic protoporphyria
scope.condition: Dermatologist-supervised low-dose solar-simulated exposure of a fixed skin site, measured before and during routine treatment
scope.comparator: Clinical model containing erythrocyte PPIX, plasma iron, exposure dose and L* but no UPE
scope.outcome: Pre-specified 24-hour phototoxic reaction defined by blinded erythema colorimetry and a standardized pain threshold

hypotheses.null_hypothesis: The UPE-augmented model improves externally validated AUC by less than 0.10 or has a non-positive lower 95% confidence bound.
hypotheses.estimand: ΔAUC = AUCclinical+initial-burst-UPE − AUCclinical for the pre-specified 24-hour phototoxic-reaction endpoint.

rationale.step: EPP involves PPIX accumulation and acute photosensitivity; in 14 patients, the post-exposure initial UPE burst correlated with plasma iron and erythrocyte PPIX and varied inversely with plasma zinc during treatment.
In human skin generally, early post-UV UPE predicted 24-hour erythema and tracked lipid-peroxidation-related photodamage.
Skin lightness materially affects UVA-induced UPE and therefore must be included in the comparator model.
Compute each model's patient-level ROC curve in a held-out centre; subtract AUCs and bootstrap by patient, declaring support only for ΔAUC≥0.10 with a positive lower confidence bound.

hypotheses.proposed_experiment: Pre-register a repeated-measures dermatology study using a safe dose ladder, fixed anatomical site, sham-exposed control site and blinded 24-hour assessment; lock the initial-burst integration window before enrollment and validate the model at a second EPP centre.
hypotheses.required_instrument: Calibrated photon-counting PMT covering 350–650 nm with second-scale acquisition in a light-tight skin chamber, plus colorimetry and a calibrated solar simulator.
hypotheses.novelty_self_claim: This tests whether UPE adds clinically actionable prediction beyond the established PPIX and iron measurements, rather than merely correlating UPE with those laboratory variables or with generic oxidative status.

hypotheses.statement: In first-ever unilateral ischemic stroke with upper-limb paresis, the simultaneous affected/unaffected hand UPE ratio measured within 14 days will add at least 0.10 to out-of-sample R² for 90-day upper-limb motor recovery beyond baseline motor score, lesion burden, skin temperature and perfusion.

scope.population: Adults with first-ever unilateral ischemic stroke and measurable upper-limb paresis, plus age-matched neurologically healthy controls
scope.condition: Simultaneous bilateral palmar measurement within 14 days of stroke after environmental acclimation and dark adaptation
scope.comparator: Prognostic model containing baseline Fugl–Meyer Upper Extremity score, imaging-derived lesion burden, skin temperature and perfusion but no UPE ratio
scope.outcome: Change in Fugl–Meyer Upper Extremity score from baseline to day 90

hypotheses.null_hypothesis: The affected/unaffected UPE ratio contributes less than 0.10 incremental external-validation R² or its coefficient is unstable in sign across validation sites.
hypotheses.estimand: Incremental R² for 90-day Fugl–Meyer improvement plus the cross-site sign consistency of the log affected/unaffected photon-radiance ratio.

rationale.step: Year-long bilateral measurements found relatively preserved left-right balance in healthy people but reported severe imbalance in some stroke patients using two PMTs spanning 300–650 nm.
Human UPE displays a diurnal rhythm, so sequential left-right measurements could convert time drift into apparent pathological asymmetry.
Human hand UPE varies by surface and individual, with palmar measurements reported as less variable in an analytical review, supporting a simultaneous within-person palmar ratio.
Calculate log(UPEaffected/UPEunaffected), add it to the locked clinical model and evaluate ΔR² in a held-out hospital; support requires ΔR²≥0.10 and the same coefficient direction at every site.

hypotheses.proposed_experiment: Use paired detectors to measure both palms concurrently at baseline, repeat at discharge for reliability, and obtain blinded day-90 motor scores; train across two stroke units and validate without recalibration at a third.
hypotheses.required_instrument: Two spectrally matched, calibrated photon-counting PMTs covering 300–650 nm with identical apertures and simultaneous acquisition, plus skin temperature and laser-Doppler perfusion sensors.
hypotheses.novelty_self_claim: This converts an old cross-sectional asymmetry observation into a prospective, within-person prognostic endpoint and explicitly tests the hidden assumption that asymmetry is not sequential-measurement or perfusion artifact.

hypotheses.statement: In fresh colorectal cancer resections, a pre-specified spontaneous UPE radiance-map classifier will identify histopathology-positive tissue regions in held-out patients with AUC at least 0.85 and sensitivity at least 0.90 at specificity at least 0.80.

scope.population: Adults undergoing primary colorectal cancer resection
scope.condition: Unfixed fresh resection slices imaged within 30 minutes in darkness without optical excitation
scope.comparator: Adjacent pathology-negative tissue from the same specimen and a gross-inspection-only baseline classifier
scope.outcome: Region-level malignant versus non-malignant status on co-registered blinded histopathology

hypotheses.null_hypothesis: Patient-held-out AUC is below 0.85, or sensitivity is below 0.90 when specificity is fixed at 0.80.
hypotheses.estimand: Patient-clustered external-validation AUC and sensitivity at the pre-specified 0.80-specificity operating point.

rationale.step: A small human-tissue study reported mean spontaneous emission of 982±513 counts/min/cm² in tumor tissue versus 625±419 in normal tissue, but used frozen samples and unequal small groups.

Cell-line and mouse experiments reported increased tumor UPE and 90% discrimination from temporal spectral-power-density configurations, but did not establish performance on fresh human surgical specimens.
Calibrated EMCCD photon counting has demonstrated visible-light detection below 30 photons/s/cm², placing spatial imaging of reported biological fluxes within current detector capability.

Partition data strictly by patient, lock preprocessing and thresholds in the training set, then compute clustered ROC statistics against co-registered histology; failure of either operating threshold kills the claim.

hypotheses.proposed_experiment: Prospectively collect consecutive resections, image dark-adapted fresh slices for a fixed duration, co-register the radiance map with whole-mount histology, and validate a locked spatial-temporal classifier in specimens from a second hospital.
hypotheses.required_instrument: Cryogenically cooled photon-counting EMCCD covering approximately 350–800 nm with calibrated collection optics and a light-tight specimen chamber.
hypotheses.novelty_self_claim: Unlike H3, this uses spontaneous rather than excitation-induced delayed luminescence; unlike H11, it demands patient-held-out clinical margin classification rather than merely showing state-related spectral information.

hypotheses.statement: For a locked type-2-diabetes UPE model, wavelength- and area-calibrated radiance measurements will achieve cross-instrument ICC of at least 0.80 and limit the loss of external predictive R² to at most 0.05 when the model is transferred between PMT and EMCCD systems, whereas raw detector counts will not.

scope.population: Adults with type 2 diabetes starting treatment, sampled across at least three clinical centres
scope.condition: Duplicate same-site hand measurements on calibrated PMT and EMCCD systems after identical acclimation and dark adaptation
scope.comparator: Raw-count harmonization without wavelength-dependent quantum-efficiency, aperture-area and dark-noise correction
scope.outcome: Agreement of UPE features and transfer performance for predicting 12-week HbA1c change

hypotheses.null_hypothesis: Calibrated cross-instrument ICC is below 0.80, calibrated cross-device predictive R² loss exceeds 0.05, or calibration does not outperform raw-count harmonization.
hypotheses.estimand: ICC for calibrated radiance features and ΔR²transfer = R²same-device − R²cross-device, compared between calibrated and raw-count pipelines.

rationale.step: The clinical literature identifies extremely low intensity, thermal and optical confounds, and absence of standardized protocols as central barriers to UPE biomarker validation.
Human UPE studies use both PMTs and CCD cameras under differing analytical conditions, making detector portability a hidden requirement for clinical deployment.
EMCCD work shows that detector noise, sampling time and wavelength-dependent quantum efficiency govern detectivity and can be addressed through calibration experiments.
A defined two-band diabetes UPE feature and a later HbA1c endpoint provide a concrete model on which to test portability.

For each feature, compute cross-instrument ICC after calibration; train the outcome model on one detector class and evaluate it unchanged on the other, with support requiring ICC≥0.80, R² loss≤0.05 and improvement over the raw-count pipeline.
Clinical biomarker validation presupposes calibrated instruments and standardized protocols.

hypotheses.proposed_experiment: Circulate the same traceable reference source among centres, measure each participant consecutively on both detector classes, convert counts to photons/s/cm² within fixed spectral bands, freeze the diabetes-response model, and perform bidirectional PMT-to-EMCCD and EMCCD-to-PMT transfer tests.
hypotheses.required_instrument: A calibrated photon-counting PMT and a cooled photon-counting EMCCD covering 400–650 nm, each characterized with the same traceable reference light source and wavelength-dependent quantum-efficiency curve.
hypotheses.novelty_self_claim: This directly tests the unregistered hidden assumption behind every clinical UPE claim: that a biomarker expressed as calibrated radiance is transportable across detector classes and sites rather than being an instrument-specific count signature.
